data.name: Iscah
data.gender_notes: Iscah is used as a unisex name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: The name Iscah is derived from the Hebrew word ‘eschah’ which means reward or recompense. In the Bible, Iscah is the name of a woman mentioned in the book of Genesis as the wife of Eliezer, the servant of Abraham. The name Iscah carries the meaning “Reward of God” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew. Parents who choose Iscah usually hope their child will grow to embody reward of god and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Iscah belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Reward of God.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Iscah total 4, giving a life-path number of 4. Number 4 is linked with Rahu and with the qualities of stability, discipline and hard work.

data.cultural_impact: The name Iscah has a rich cultural significance, as it is derived from the Hebrew language which was widely used in the ancient Middle East. At that time, names held great importance in expressing one's identity and heritage. Iscah is a rare and obscure name, which adds to its unique character.
data.spiritual_significance: The spiritual significance of the name Iscah lies in its biblical roots. In the Bible, Iscah's marriage to Eliezer, a servant of Abraham, symbolizes the faithful and devoted servant who is rewarded for their loyalty and dedication. This suggests that the name Iscah may hold a deeper meaning for those seeking spiritual growth and a greater understanding of the rewards of faith and loyalty.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Iscah, meaning "reward of God," serves as a reminder of the divine blessings bestowed upon us throughout our lives. It encourages faith in God's plan and trust in His provision.

historical_references.context: The name Iscah (אישכה) is given to the well that Abraham's servant found after promising Rebekah that the next person who asked for a drink would be the man who would marry her. This well was near the city of Gerar.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Joshua 15:33 The name Iscah carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Iscah is a town in the territory allotted to the tribe of Judah.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Iscah is a biblical Hebrew name meaning 'restraint' or 'binding'. It is found in the Old Testament as the name of the wife of Abraham and the mother of Esau and Jacob. Today, this name is not commonly used but is seen on various platforms. It is featured on baby names websites for those seeking unique and less common names. On Judaic websites and forums, it is appreciated by those with an interest in Jewish heritage and history. Additionally, it is mentioned on historical and archaeological websites in discussions about the ancient Middle East and its people.
